This year can be said to be the year of super apps. OpenAI recently launched its own super app and admitted that the app is "a bit messy." Meanwhile, Microsoft's CEO also confirmed that a super app will be rolled out for Copilot in the near future.

Microsoft Copilot "Super App" to integrate Cowork, chat, coding and other features

Microsoft is developing an AI "super app" that integrates Copilot's chat, coding, and intelligent agent features. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said at Wednesday's earnings call that the app will be launched this year, covering "consumer and business experiences." Nadella pointed out: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat features to Cowork and then to Autopilots. This quarter, we are integrating these Copilot experiences, including coding features, into a single super app... This is a major advancement, and I look forward to sharing more details later."

OpenAI's process of launching its own "super app" has turned into a mess, but that clearly hasn't stopped other companies from continuing to adopt the super app strategy.

Perhaps Microsoft can build an all-in-one app more effectively and avoid repeating OpenAI's mistakes.

That said, CEO Nadella also recently stated that the company is transitioning from apps and focusing on intelligent agents. The AI era is still in its early stages, and the trends and best practices for building AI-centric interfaces are still constantly evolving.

As for Apple, there are no signs of a shift toward super apps; instead, it continues to launch independent and specialized new apps. It remains to be seen whether this strategy will change in the future.

What do you think of the recent "super app" trend? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
